_meta.indication: Treatment of patients with cystic fibrosis (CF) aged 12 years and older who are homozygous for the F508del mutation or who have at least one mutation in the CFTR gene that is responsive to tezacaftor/ivacaftor based on in vitro data and/or clinical evidence

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study with a 24-week treatment period; subjects randomized 1:1 to TEZ/IVA or placebo
pivotal_trials.population: CF patients aged 12 years and older who are homozygous for the F508del mutation in the CFTR gene
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Absolute change from baseline in percent predicted FEV1 (ppFEV1) through Week 24
pivotal_trials.n: 504 in the Full Analysis Set (248 TEZ/IVA, 256 placebo)
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean absolute change in ppFEV1 through Week 24 was -0.6 for placebo vs 3.4 for TEZ/IVA; treatment difference from placebo 4.0 percentage points (95% CI 3.1, 4.8), p<0.0001. Pulmonary exacerbation rate ratio vs placebo 0.65 (95% CI 0.48, 0.88), p=0.0054.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 2-period, 3-treatment crossover study with 8-week treatment periods (TEZ/IVA, IVA monotherapy, placebo)
pivotal_trials.population: CF patients aged 12 years and older heterozygous for the F508del mutation with a second allele carrying a residual-function CFTR mutation predicted to be responsive to TEZ/IVA
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Absolute change in ppFEV1 from baseline to the average of Week 4 and Week 8 measurements in each treatment period
pivotal_trials.n: 244 in the Full Analysis Set (placebo N=161, IVA N=156, TEZ/IVA N=161 across crossover periods)
pivotal_trials.result: Absolute change in ppFEV1 treatment difference vs placebo 6.8 (95% CI 5.7, 7.8) and vs IVA monotherapy 2.1 (95% CI 1.2, 2.9), demonstrating contribution of TEZ

key_safety: Most common adverse drug reactions (≥3% and greater than placebo) were headache (15% vs 13%), nausea (9% vs 7%), sinus congestion (4% vs 2%), and dizziness (4% vs 2%). Most serious AEs were pulmonary exacerbations of CF (~7% TEZ/IVA vs 10% placebo). Transaminase elevations noted with SYMDEKO or ivacaftor.
target_moa: Tezacaftor is a CFTR corrector that facilitates cellular processing and trafficking of normal and select mutant CFTR (including F508del-CFTR) to increase mature CFTR at the cell surface; ivacaftor is a CFTR potentiator that increases chloride transport by potentiating the channel-open probability (gating) of CFTR at the cell surface
modality: Small molecule (fixed/co-packaged combination of two small-molecule CFTR modulators)
companion_dx_detail: No companion diagnostic required; CDRH noted several FDA-cleared diagnostic tests are available to detect the F508del mutation, and responsiveness of less common mutations may be established by in vitro (Ussing chamber) assay data

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held; a PADAC meeting was considered but the Division decided the evidence supporting approval was sufficiently robust that AC discussion was not necessary

description.text: Expanded indication to cystic fibrosis patients aged 6 to less than 12 years homozygous for F508del or with at least one CFTR mutation responsive to tezacaftor/ivacaftor

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for expansion of the indication for the use of tezacaftor/ivacaftor 50 mg/75 mg once daily followed by ivacaftor 75 mg 12 hours later for patients < 30 kg, and tezacaftor/ivacaftor 100 mg/150 mg once daily followed by ivacaftor 150 mg 12 hours later for patients ≥ 30 kg, for the treatment of cystic fibrosis in patients aged 6 to less than 12 years old who are homozygous for the *F508del* mutation or who have at least one mutation in the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (*CFTR*) gene that is responsive to tezacaftor/ivacaftor based on *in vitro* data and/or clinical evidence.

description.text: Expanded Cystic Fibrosis indication to include additional responsive CFTR gene mutations based on in vitro data

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for an expansion of the indicated Cystic Fibrosis patient population to include additional mutations in the *CFTR* gene that have been identified as responsive to tezacaftor/ivacaftor based upon *in vitro* data.

To support this application, Vertex has completed three phase 3 efficacy and safety trials in three different CFTR mutation subpopulations. These studies demonstrated substantial evidence of efficacy for the TEZ/IVA combination in CF patients who are homozygous for the *F508del* mutation (Trial 106), those with missense mutations predicted to be responsive to TEZ/IVA (Trial 108), and those with certain non-canonical splice mutations for which clinical data were available (Trial 108). Efficacy was not established for CFTR mutations predicted to be non-responsive to the TEZ/IVA combination (Trial 107).
